verdict: No blocking issue for actual normal LF-delimited QEMU CPU dumps; two strictness limitations below.
checks: aarch64_cpu_dump_state emits11 register lines: PC/X00/X01, nine tripletsX02..X28, X29/X30/SP, then PSTATE footer. Parser requires12 lines and all31 GPRs, PC, SP exactly once.
log_cpu_exec holds qemu_log_trylock through cpu_dump_state and unlock; no inter-dump pairing is inferred. This does not establish guest thread/process identity.
Offsets accumulate original byte lengths and raw block SHA preserves retained bytes. Unexpected interleaving line is retained and invalidates block.
Only complete exact entryPC96df690 and finalPC96e219c receive low32 ABI interpretation. UnknownPC retains fields without ABI; incomplete blocks excluded from distributions.
No unchanged token/flags at return or entry/return pairing is asserted. Kernel slide/build/filter/control provenance remains independently required.

limitations.detail: PSTATE eight hexadecimal digits followed by arbitrary non-newline suffix is accepted; flags/EL suffix is not validated against actual formatter. Hence exact original-layout claim applies more strongly to registers than footer.
Bare CR is treated as a line separator; offsets remain byte-correct, but this is not physical-LF-only framing. Actual dump formatter emits LF.

validation_scope: Read-only source review against f37-identical cpu.c/cpu-exec.c; reused existing owned-attempt6 evidence, no new test execution or VM action.
